questions.question: What is the difference between Git and GitHub?
options: Git is a version control tool; GitHub is a cloud platform to host Git repositories
questions.correct_answer: Git is a version control tool; GitHub is a cloud platform to host Git repositories
questions.explanation: Git tracks changes locally on your machine. GitHub is a web-based platform where you store, share, and collaborate on Git repos.

questions.question: What does git push -u origin main do?
options: Deletes the main branch on GitHub
Pushes commits and sets origin/main as the upstream tracking branch
Creates a new branch on GitHub
questions.correct_answer: Pushes commits and sets origin/main as the upstream tracking branch
questions.explanation: -u sets the upstream so future 'git push' and 'git pull' commands work without specifying remote and branch each time.

questions.question: What is a Fork on GitHub?
options: Your own copy of someone else's repository under your account
questions.correct_answer: Your own copy of someone else's repository under your account
questions.explanation: Forking copies a repo to your GitHub account, letting you make changes freely without affecting the original project.

questions.question: What is a Pull Request on GitHub?
options: A proposal to merge a branch with code review and discussion before merging
Pulling the latest code from remote
questions.correct_answer: A proposal to merge a branch with code review and discussion before merging
questions.explanation: PRs are the collaboration mechanism — teammates can review, comment, request changes, and approve before code is merged.

questions.question: What does 'Squash and merge' do to a Pull Request?
options: Combines all PR commits into a single commit before merging
questions.correct_answer: Combines all PR commits into a single commit before merging
questions.explanation: Squash and merge collapses all feature branch commits (including WIP commits) into one clean commit on main.

questions.question: How do you automatically close a GitHub issue when a PR is merged?
options: Add the issue number to the branch name
questions.explanation: Keywords like 'Closes #12', 'Fixes #12', or 'Resolves #12' in PR descriptions automatically close the linked issue when the PR merges.

questions.question: Where do GitHub Actions workflow files live?
questions.explanation: GitHub automatically detects and executes YAML workflow files placed in the .github/workflows/ directory.

questions.question: What does 'needs: test' in a GitHub Actions job mean?
options: The job only runs after the 'test' job completes successfully
The job skips if tests fail
The job runs in parallel with test
questions.correct_answer: The job only runs after the 'test' job completes successfully
questions.explanation: 'needs' creates a sequential dependency — the deploy job runs only if the test job succeeds, preventing broken deployments.

questions.question: What is the 'upstream' remote in a forked repository workflow?
options: The original repository you forked from
questions.correct_answer: The original repository you forked from
questions.explanation: Adding the original repo as 'upstream' lets you sync your fork with new changes from the original project.

questions.question: Which GitHub issue label should beginners look for to find approachable issues?
questions.explanation: 'good first issue' is a standard GitHub label maintainers use to mark issues suitable for newcomers to the project.

questions.question: What are GitHub Secrets used for?
options: Storing sensitive values like passwords and tokens for use in GitHub Actions
questions.correct_answer: Storing sensitive values like passwords and tokens for use in GitHub Actions
questions.explanation: GitHub Secrets securely stores credentials accessible as ${{ secrets.NAME }} in workflows without exposing them in code or logs.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a GitHub Actions trigger 'on: pull_request'?
options: Runs the workflow when a PR is merged only
Runs the workflow when a PR is opened or updated
Triggers only for PRs to main branch
questions.correct_answer: Runs the workflow when a PR is opened or updated
questions.explanation: on: pull_request triggers the workflow whenever a PR is opened, synchronized (new commits pushed), or reopened.

questions.question: What does git clone do?
options: Copies a remote repository to your local machine with full history
questions.correct_answer: Copies a remote repository to your local machine with full history
questions.explanation: git clone downloads the entire repository including all branches and commit history to your local machine.

questions.question: What is a GitHub Project (Kanban board)?
options: A project management board to track issues and PRs visually
questions.correct_answer: A project management board to track issues and PRs visually
questions.explanation: GitHub Projects provides a Kanban-style board to organize issues and PRs across columns like Todo, In Progress, and Done.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a Draft Pull Request?
options: To signal work in progress not yet ready for review
questions.correct_answer: To signal work in progress not yet ready for review
questions.explanation: Draft PRs allow early feedback and visibility on ongoing work without requesting a full review until the code is ready.
